A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dependability of a robot is not only a consequence of its design but also of its use and that the dependability is not an absolute property of a robot but rather a relative one, i.e. it is relative to the task to be performed and the user of the robot.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the dependability of intelligent humanoid robots can be improved significantly if the following principles are applied: (i) the robot is designed for easy maintenance and repair; (ii) the robot has a high degree of modularity; (iii) the robot is equipped with an extensive set of sensors and actuators; (iv) the robot has an extensive software infrastructure; (v) the robot has to be tested extensively.
dependability is not an obstacle for building intelligent robots, but it is a consequence of good design and a necessary prerequisite for successful long term operation of service robots.
dependability can be significantly improved by a proper design of the robot and by the careful selection and integration of its components.
